organisation.narrative: Australia - Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade

description.narrative: Research by Amnesty International in 2018 established that women and girls were subject to very high levels of online abuse simply because of their gender. Women, particularly those in leadership positions or who are required to maintain an online presence as part of their professional lives, face unacceptably high levels of gender-based abuse online. ‍ To address this issue, DFAT invested $350,000 in a three-year project run by Australia’s eSafety Commissioner to increase online safety in Fiji. Upon project completion in March 2024, eSafety’s activities enabled Fiji’s Online Safety Commission to develop and implement effective online safety measures. This was achieved through a combination of influencing policy; capacity building of frontline service providers; enhanced reporting and investigation mechanisms; public awareness campaigns and advocacy; and incorporation of online safety principles into the education curriculum.

Two-phased cyber security exercises were delivered by Retrospect Labs to improve the baseline cyber security capability of critical infrastructure for government and critical infrastructure providers, equipping them with the skills and knowledge to respond effectively to a broad range of cyber threats in Samoa, Vanuatu and Tonga. ‍ Phase one focused on providing government and critical infrastructure organisations with baseline skills and knowledge to institute key Incident Response concepts, policies, and processes. ‍ Phase two built on phase one, putting skills and knowledge into practice, through a guided, hands-on exercise where participants had to respond to a simulated Incident Response Guided Live Fire Exercises. ‍ The program’s success was evidenced by strong participant engagement and positive post-delivery feedback with 100% of participants strongly agreeing or agreeing the course improved their knowledge and understanding of the application of international law in cyber-space. The DFAT funded initiative was undertaken over multiple years and involved 58 government agencies and 35 private/community service organisations across the three countries.

Under DFAT’s Southeast Asia and Pacific Cyber program, between January and June 2025 Cyber Law International delivered capacity building programs in Southeast Asia to improve the understanding of the application of international law in cyberspace. Partnering with The Netherlands’ Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Singapore’s Cyber Security Agency, the initiative delivered four executive courses and three alumni workshops, training 143 participants from all ten ASEAN countries. ‍ Evaluation data confirmed lasting improvements in participants' ability to apply international law to cyber operations. This shared understanding is critical to achieve international cyber stability, fostering protection of human rights online, and ensuring that cyberspace is governed and safeguarded by a common set of rules. ‍ Participants included legal advisers to government ministries and organisations (especially the Ministries of Foreign Affairs and Defence); practicing attorneys from Attorney Generals’ Offices, Ministries of Justice and the Judiciary; policy experts; diplomats; law enforcement personnel and individuals responsible for planning and approving cyber operations. Anecdotally, the program’s impact has likely extended beyond the immediate participants and indirectly benefited participants’ colleagues within the same agencies and their broader government departments.
